verdict_line: Record revenue, operating margin up 240 basis points and intermodal volume up 9% — a railroad executing well, which makes the efficiency pitch harder. Strong intermodal alignment, no named technology owner yet.

thesis.text: This is a strong quarter, not a distressed one. Record revenue of $3.94 billion (+10%), operating income $1.51 billion (+17%), operating margin 38.3% (+240bps), diluted EPS $0.54 (+23%).
Intermodal is the growth engine — volume up 9% within total volume growth of 6% to 1.68 million units. Direct alignment with the Intermodal-as-Horizontal pillar.

Cash generation transformed. H1 free cash flow before dividends of $1.62 billion against $444 million in the prior year, with FY2026 guidance of over 80% free cash flow growth and capex held below $2.4 billion.
Safety improved sharply — FRA injury rate down 19% and train accident rate down 30% year over year, closing the safety-remediation wedge.

exhibits.title: Q2 2026 performance
exhibits.headline: Record revenue with 240 basis points of margin expansion — CSX is executing, so the entry point is growth, not repair.
exhibits.body_html:
Revenue $3.94 billion (record, +10%), operating income $1.51 billion (+17%), operating margin 38.3% (+240bps), net earnings $1.00 billion (+21%), diluted EPS $0.54 (+23%). Volume 1.68 million units (+6%) with intermodal volume up 9%. First-half free cash flow before dividends $1.62 billion against $444 million. FY2026 guidance: mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth, over 350 basis points of operating-margin expansion, over 80% free cash flow growth, capex below $2.4 billion. CEO: Steve Angel.

CSX is also a 19.78% owner of TTX and a stakeholder in the UP-NS merger proceedings — see the TTX and Union Pacific baselines.
exhibits.sowhat: With margin expanding and cash generation transformed, CSX has money and no crisis. The credible approach is intermodal growth capacity and pricing science — helping them capture more of a segment already growing 9% — rather than cost repair.
